lines.text: What if Earth suddenly doubled in size?
Same rock, same density, but eight times the mass.
Instantly, gravity doubles. A seventy kilo athlete now carries a hundred and forty.
Sprinters crumple off the blocks, and the high jumper can barely leave the ground.
Tall trees topple under their own weight.
And any animal bigger than a dog risks breaking a leg just by running.
A bigger Earth also spins thirty two times slower, so one day lasts more than a month.
One side bakes for weeks while the other freezes, whipping up storms that flatten buildings.
The air is twice as dense, but still breathable.
Flying gets easier, but landing is brutal, so birds touch down on water.
A bigger planet traps more heat inside, and hundreds of new volcanoes erupt.
Their gases could trigger a runaway greenhouse, and the biggest extinction Earth has ever seen.
Over thousands of generations, survivors grow low and wide. Sturdy plants, thick-legged animals, and shorter, stronger people.
The stadium fills again, with athletes who never knew the old world.
So, would you survive the first day?
